stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its position at time t hours is \( x(t) = t \left(t - 1\right)^{2} \), for \( 0 \le t \le 5 \). Find all open intervals of time in \( 0 < t < 5 \) during which the particle is moving to the right. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The particle is moving to the right exactly on \( \left(0, \frac{1}{3}\right) \) and \( \left(1, 5\right) \), because \( v(t) > 0 \) there.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the position with the product rule: \( v(t) = x'(t) = \left(t - 1\right) \left(3 t - 1\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: velocity is the derivative of position

worked_solution.text: Solving \( v(t) = 0 \) gives \( t = \frac{1}{3}, 1 \), which split \( 0 < t < 5 \) into pieces on which v keeps one sign.

Testing a time in each piece shows \( v(t) > 0 \) exactly on \( \left(0, \frac{1}{3}\right) \) and \( \left(1, 5\right) \). The particle moves to the right when its velocity is positive, so it moves to the right on \( \left(0, \frac{1}{3}\right) \) and \( \left(1, 5\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of velocity gives the direction of motion

options.label: The particle is moving to the right exactly on \( \left(\frac{2}{3}, 5\right) \), because v(t) is increasing there.
options.derivation: the direction read from whether the velocity is increasing, the sign of its change, rather than from its sign

options.label: The particle is moving to the right exactly on \( \left(0, \frac{1}{3}\right) \) and \( \left(1, 5\right) \), because \( v(t) > 0 \) there.
The particle is moving to the right exactly on \( \left(0, 1\right) \) and \( \left(1, 5\right) \), because \( x(t) > 0 \) there.
options.derivation: the direction read from the sign of the position x(t) rather than of the velocity

options.label: The particle is moving to the right exactly on \( \left(1, 5\right) \), because \( v(t) > 0 \) there.
options.derivation: only the integer zero t = 1 found by trying whole-number times, so the zero at t = 1/3 is missed and each remaining piece is judged at one whole-number time
